title: Toppings: CPU-Assisted, Rank-Aware Adapter Serving for LLM Inference
problem: Serving multiple LLM adapters (parameter-efficient fine-tuned models) concurrently during inference incurs significant memory and scheduling overhead, creating contention on GPU resources and degrading throughput when handling diverse adapter requests simultaneously.
motivation: Production LLM services require efficient deployment of personalized model variants through adapters without sacrificing latency or throughput.
method: Toppings employs a CPU-assisted serving architecture where the CPU handles adapter scheduling, routing decisions, and memory management based on rank-aware prioritization, while GPUs focus on compute-heavy inference operations. The rank-aware component dynamically prioritizes adapters based on request characteristics or adapter importance metrics. CPU handles adapter lookup, batching decisions, and memory movement overhead between CPU/GPU memory, reducing GPU idle cycles and enabling higher adapter concurrency.
key_novelty: Rank-aware adapter scheduling that offloads memory and routing overhead to CPU, allowing GPUs to maximize inference throughput for multi-adapter workloads.
contributions: CPU-assisted adapter serving system architecture for concurrent LLM adapter deployment
Rank-aware scheduling algorithm for prioritizing adapters based on request characteristics
Memory co-location strategy leveraging CPU-GPU hierarchy for adapter management
Demonstrated throughput and latency improvements on multi-adapter inference benchmarks
limitations: Scalability and applicability to very large adapter counts or specific adapter types not discussed.
